gates.claim: Identity and documentation describe a retained product capability.
gates.contract: The capability has a named requirement and applicable accepted decisions.
gates.evidence: Trace the published claim to its owner, decision status, target and candidate-specific evidence.
gates.refusal: Mark proposed or unverified behavior as such; do not publish it as shipped.

gates.claim: File safety, recovery or sync is accepted for a retained adapter.
gates.contract: The applicable file, recovery and trust requirements and decisions are identified.
gates.evidence: Map adapter guarantees and fault scenarios to accepted decisions and exact-candidate results.
gates.refusal: An open writer or trust decision cannot establish a stronger safety guarantee.

gates.claim: A model connection, credential or usage behavior is supported.
gates.contract: The applicable privacy, provider and cost requirements have owners and accepted policy.
gates.evidence: Record the selected connection and target, decision state, capability tests and known or unknown charges.
gates.refusal: Do not present an undecided policy, catalog entry or unknown charge as verified support.

gates.claim: An editor, library or import journey preserves the author's work.
gates.contract: The target adapter implements the applicable checked save, conflict, recovery and publication contract.
gates.evidence: Exercise create, import, edit, reopen, conflicts and failed publication on the claimed adapter.
gates.refusal: Refuse unsupported or unsafe imports and never call an unconfirmed write saved.

gates.claim: Agent edits or durable workflow state are accepted.
gates.contract: The Library writer supplies checked publication, conflict handling and recoverable state for the claimed artifacts.
gates.evidence: Test concurrent author edits, failed commits, interruption and recovery through the actual publisher.
gates.refusal: Do not claim adoption or recovery on an uncertain or unchecked write.

gates.claim: An agent turn or workflow uses a model connection.
gates.contract: The selected route supplies scoped credentials, capability, attribution and truthful usage boundaries.
gates.evidence: Exercise selection, permission, dispatch, cancellation and reported or unknown charges for the claimed route.
gates.refusal: No silent provider substitution, inferred free call or dispatch without applicable authority.

gates.claim: Bible or series records are edited and reopened within a book.
gates.contract: Book identity, library navigation and saved editor state identify the correct owner and source.
gates.evidence: Round-trip planning records with the selected book, reopen and exercise changed or unavailable sources.
gates.refusal: Do not attach records to an ambiguous book or claim an unsaved edit persisted.

gates.claim: An agent reads or proposes changes to Bible or series records.
gates.contract: Agent access is scoped to authorized sources and proposed changes use checked author-controlled publication.
gates.evidence: Test granted and excluded sources, reviewed proposals, conflicts and interruption.
gates.refusal: A book grant is not blanket series access; do not publish an unreviewed or stale proposal.

gates.claim: History, notes or goals are stored, restored or removed.
gates.contract: Checked writes, version/hash conflict handling and recoverable deletion protect the relevant files.
gates.evidence: Exercise failed and concurrent writes, checked restore and recovery on each claimed adapter.
gates.refusal: Do not overwrite a changed source or claim a history restore without a confirmed receipt.

gates.claim: A history entry, goal or note refers to a saved book or chapter.
gates.contract: Stable book/chapter identity and the exact saved source are available to the owner.
gates.evidence: Test renames, reopened books, source hashes and stale anchors against saved content.
gates.refusal: Show stale or unavailable sources; do not silently relocate a note or count unsaved text.

gates.claim: A deterministic review reports or navigates manuscript evidence.
gates.contract: The editor and library supply exact saved chapter identity, bytes and current-source navigation.
gates.evidence: Repeat analysis on saved bytes and test exact navigation, source changes and missing chapters.
gates.refusal: Show stale, incomplete or unavailable evidence instead of inventing a location.

gates.claim: A reader or continuity run sends selected material or applies a suggestion.
gates.contract: Explicit scoped review authority, read-only generation and separate checked application are maintained.
gates.evidence: Test consent, included and excluded sources, cancellation, attribution and separately approved application.
gates.refusal: Do not send outside the grant, mutate during review or apply stale suggestions silently.

gates.claim: A structured reader uses deterministic findings or source-linked report evidence.
gates.contract: Saved-source identity, exact finding association, coverage and staleness remain traceable.
gates.evidence: Verify the cited source span and finding identity, including changed sources and incomplete coverage.
gates.refusal: Do not present an unmatched finding or subjective reader judgment as a verified metric.

gates.claim: An illustration or cover asset is saved or replaced.
gates.contract: The asset and its manifest use recoverable publication and preserve the original on failure.
gates.evidence: Inject asset and manifest write failures, reopen the book and verify original and recoverable bytes.
gates.refusal: Do not report a saved asset when publication is uncertain or discard a received result.

gates.claim: An illustration or cover is attached to a book or chapter.
gates.contract: Book and chapter identity and saved manuscript context bind the selected asset to its owner.
gates.evidence: Test asset selection, attachment, reopening and changed or missing source identities.
gates.refusal: Do not attach to the wrong owner or imply an unsaved selection is the exported asset.

gates.claim: A formatted export represents the author's book.
gates.contract: The export uses the ordered, identified saved manuscript snapshot and applicable matter.
gates.evidence: Compare exported content and order with the saved source, including unsaved changes and source failures.
gates.refusal: Do not present a partial or unsaved snapshot as a complete verified book.

gates.claim: A publishing or export claim depends on a selected cover or its target geometry.
gates.contract: The chosen cover asset, provenance and applicable measured target inputs are available to export.
gates.evidence: Match the exported asset and independently measured dimensions to the selected saved cover and target.
gates.refusal: Mark missing cover or measurements unknown and withhold cover-dependent readiness; unrelated exports may proceed.

gates.claim: Voice input or output uses a selected provider connection.
gates.contract: The explicit route supplies capability, credential isolation and cost or unknown-charge disclosure.
gates.evidence: Exercise route selection, unsupported models, refusal, request attribution and uncertain charges.
gates.refusal: Do not silently switch to another paid route or describe an unknown charge as zero.

gates.claim: Voice controls or submits an agent interaction.
gates.contract: The bound session respects the current mode, source, permission, stop and explicit submission authority.
gates.evidence: Exercise bound activation, interruption, revoked authority, stop and exact submitted words end to end.
gates.refusal: Unconfirmed speech remains unsubmitted; a stop or unavailable host must not imply a completed turn.

gates.claim: Audiobook source, cast, generated chapters or package are persisted.
gates.contract: Source versions and output records use checked, recoverable storage without replacing the manuscript.
gates.evidence: Test stale sources, failed publication, partial chapter results and explicit recovery.
gates.refusal: Do not claim a complete package or replay uncertain work after an unconfirmed save.

gates.claim: A narrator or character chapter is auditioned or generated with speech services.
gates.contract: Explicit speech routes, background boundaries, author consent and truthful request settlement apply.
gates.evidence: Test selected voice, approved script, cancellation, unknown charges and partial failures for each claimed route.
gates.refusal: Do not start an unapproved paid batch, silently retry or promise identical rerendered audio.

gates.claim: Routing or spend policy describes an available model or price.
gates.contract: Provider capability, connection identity and price freshness or uncertainty come from the model contract.
gates.evidence: Test unavailable routes, stale prices, unknown usage and actual model attribution.
gates.refusal: Do not turn a catalog estimate or unknown charge into a guaranteed strict cap.

gates.claim: A policy is admitted into an agent workflow or dispatch.
gates.contract: Pinned roles and destinations are constrained by the workflow grant and its admission mode.
gates.evidence: Exercise permission, selected roles, admission, settlement and cancellation without side effects in preview.
gates.refusal: No automatic retry, fallback or dispatch beyond the grant; an advisory preview is not enforcement.

gates.claim: CLI or MCP clients read, write, undo or delete book content.
gates.contract: The same checked Library writer, recoverable deletion and conflict rules apply to external clients.
gates.evidence: Exercise client writes, stale baselines, undo and failures against the actual backend.
gates.refusal: Reject unchecked or unauthorized mutation and retain conflicting author data.

gates.claim: An external client invokes the studio agent tool catalog.
gates.contract: Tool tiers, disabled tools, explicit write opt-in and destructive approval match agent authority.
gates.evidence: Independent clients test reads, disabled tools, write opt-in, approvals and unauthorized requests.
gates.refusal: Do not expose a disabled or unapproved write merely because the client can connect.

gates.claim: Browser storage claims save, conflict or recovery behavior.
gates.contract: Each supported browser adapter preserves the shared file protocol and discloses its actual limits.
gates.evidence: Run storage, quota, permission, conflict and recovery checks on the claimed browser/adapter matrix.
gates.refusal: Report unconfirmed saves and unsupported atomicity; do not call browser storage a backup.

gates.claim: A browser connects to a provider or stores a credential.
gates.contract: Provider-specific direct browser access and origin-local credential disclosure govern the route.
gates.evidence: Verify the claimed browser/provider combination, credential removal and unavailable-provider refusal.
gates.refusal: Do not proxy prose or secrets or claim a desktop-only route works in the browser.

gates.claim: The browser offers a library, editor or import journey.
gates.contract: Shared identity, saved-source and import boundaries apply on the supported browser surface.
gates.evidence: Exercise open, edit, reopen and each claimed import with real browser storage and permissions.
gates.refusal: Refuse unavailable import or filesystem operations instead of implying desktop parity.

gates.claim: A browser surface offers an agent mode or tool.
gates.contract: The selected host enforces the same applicable authority, source scope and checked publication rules.
gates.evidence: Exercise supported browser operations and permission, cancellation and unsupported-host paths.
gates.refusal: Refuse unavailable agent actions before request or write; shared UI is not runtime proof.

gates.claim: An iPhone or iPad surface reuses shared editor or capability behavior.
gates.contract: Shared operation-level capabilities and storage/refusal boundaries are adapted to the native host.
gates.evidence: Exercise each claimed operation with native storage, lifecycle and permission evidence on the supported device matrix.
gates.refusal: A responsive layout or Simulator alone does not establish native storage or release support.

gates.claim: An iPhone or iPad claim includes voice input, output or control.
gates.contract: The mobile host enforces voice permission, bound session, source and stop boundaries.
gates.evidence: Record approved native permission, interruption and actual input/output checks for each claimed device.
gates.refusal: Mark unqualified voice unavailable; do not infer microphone behavior from a simulated layout.

gates.claim: Android claims a shared editor, storage or provider operation.
gates.contract: Shared per-operation capabilities and refusal semantics are implemented behind accepted Android host boundaries.
gates.evidence: Test the claimed Android adapter, permission, lifecycle and recovery on its supported device matrix.
gates.refusal: Unaccepted storage or credential decisions do not authorize writes or a release claim.

gates.claim: An Android capability claim includes voice input, output or control.
gates.contract: The selected Android host must honor voice permissions, bound source/session and stop semantics.
gates.evidence: Verify the accepted voice boundary and real-device permission, interruption and input/output behavior for claimed devices.
gates.refusal: Refuse or omit voice from an Android slice until qualified; storage/editor work may proceed independently.

gates.claim: A glasses interaction uses a phone companion.
gates.contract: The selected phone host owns the approved companion lifecycle and private device boundary.
gates.evidence: Verify the accepted phone/companion path and disconnection or permission failures on claimed hardware.
gates.refusal: A phone mock or responsive screen cannot establish a connected companion claim.

gates.claim: A glasses or companion claim includes speech interaction.
gates.contract: Voice requests use explicit host permission, bound session and truthful stop/settlement behavior.
gates.evidence: Exercise the approved interaction, interruption, privacy and unavailable-host paths on claimed hardware.
gates.refusal: Do not imply always-listening capture or live voice without a qualified and authorized path.

gates.claim: A companion invokes a studio tool or action.
gates.contract: The authenticated tool boundary preserves read/write tiers, approval, disabled tools and undo.
gates.evidence: Test private transport, rejected origins or tokens and approved versus refused actions end to end.
gates.refusal: Do not expose a personal library or destructive action over an unapproved transport.

gates.claim: A desktop package is identified or documented as a product release.
gates.contract: Visible identity and release documentation preserve compatible profile and internal identities.
gates.evidence: Inspect package metadata, user-visible links and existing-profile continuity on the candidate.
gates.refusal: Do not rename protected identities or advertise an artifact not actually qualified.

gates.claim: Installation, upgrade or recovery preserves a desktop library.
gates.contract: Application replacement does not rewrite author data and newer schemas are refused safely.
gates.evidence: Compare library and profile before and after clean install, upgrade, failure and recovery on claimed targets.
gates.refusal: Do not report safe upgrade when library preservation or schema compatibility is unverified.

gates.claim: An installed desktop build retains a model connection or credential.
gates.contract: Protected credential storage and profile identity remain compatible across the claimed lifecycle.
gates.evidence: Test connection continuity and unavailable-vault refusal without exposing secret material.
gates.refusal: Do not migrate credentials into the library or claim protected storage where it is unavailable.

gates.claim: A desktop artifact is accepted as a release candidate.
gates.contract: Applicable quality, security and accessibility gates remain intact and candidate-specific.
gates.evidence: Record exact commit, target, artifact, gate results, failures and any authorized disposition.
gates.refusal: A prior baseline or a weakened or failing gate is not candidate release evidence.

gates.claim: A quality or security gate covers a retained requirement.
gates.contract: Requirements, decision states and acceptance owners define what the gate is meant to prove.
gates.evidence: Trace each applicable check to its requirement, target, candidate and remaining evidence gaps.
gates.refusal: Passing a structural check does not settle an open decision or prove an untested capability.

gates.claim: A guide, sample or film presents product identity and links.
gates.contract: Published names, compatibility language and destinations match the accepted identity contract.
gates.evidence: Inspect the exact artifact and destinations against the candidate's supported identity and documentation.
gates.refusal: Do not publish a broken link or imply a changed internal credential or profile identity.

gates.claim: A guide or film depicts library, import or editor behavior.
gates.contract: The depicted journey and source data match the actual supported editor and import scope.
gates.evidence: Map each shown action to its candidate, target, fixture or live boundary and verified result.
gates.refusal: Do not present fixture footage or an unsupported import as a qualified product journey.

gates.claim: A guide or film depicts an agent workflow.
gates.contract: Claims preserve the selected mode, author authority and distinction between generated and applied work.
gates.evidence: Match the recording or instructions to exercised permissions, actions and candidate-specific results.
gates.refusal: Do not present a planned autonomous capability or staged result as connected execution.

gates.claim: A guide, sample or film depicts generated or selected image assets.
gates.contract: The image's source, selection, consent and applicable attribution remain truthful.
gates.evidence: Inspect the exact asset and shot manifest, including fixture status, rights and documented provenance.
gates.refusal: Do not imply generation, authorship or export provenance that the evidence does not establish.

gates.claim: A guide or film depicts voice capture, spoken output or control.
gates.contract: The depiction respects explicit activation, selected route and the demonstrated host boundary.
gates.evidence: Review exact audio and shots against authorized capture, input/output and provenance records.
gates.refusal: Do not present staged audio or author-started capture as an always-listening capability.

gates.claim: A guide or sample documents CLI or MCP access.
gates.contract: Documented client commands preserve authentication, read-only defaults and write approvals.
gates.evidence: Exercise the documented workflow with an independent client and inspect secret-free examples.
gates.refusal: Do not publish working credentials or imply unrestricted write access.

gates.claim: The supported desktop matrix includes editor, library or import journeys.
gates.contract: Each claimed desktop journey uses the applicable saved-source, import and recovery contract.
gates.evidence: Run the exact release candidate's create, import, edit, reopen and recovery journeys for each claimed target.
gates.refusal: Exclude unsupported capability from the desktop matrix rather than claiming it passed; its retained lane stays open.

gates.claim: The supported desktop matrix includes an agent mode or workflow.
gates.contract: Claimed agent actions have scoped authority, checked publication and truthful interruption/recovery.
gates.evidence: Exercise the exact candidate's claimed modes, permissions, stop and publication outcomes.
gates.refusal: Do not extend a verified desktop slice into an unverified full-book or quality claim.

gates.claim: The supported desktop matrix includes an export or publishing readiness claim.
gates.contract: The claimed format uses the saved snapshot and only applicable measured validation inputs.
gates.evidence: Inspect candidate exports with appropriate independent tooling and record target-specific results.
gates.refusal: Do not imply external acceptance or readiness for a check that was not passed.

gates.claim: The supported desktop matrix includes a voice capability.
gates.contract: The claimed host and route satisfy explicit activation, permission, source and stop boundaries.
gates.evidence: Record candidate-specific host, route and authorized input/output evidence separately from synthetic checks.
gates.refusal: Withhold unqualified voice claims; unrelated retained targets are not desktop blockers.

gates.claim: The supported desktop matrix includes CLI or MCP access.
gates.contract: The release's external client surface enforces authentication, tool tiers and checked writes.
gates.evidence: Run independent client reads, opted-in writes, approvals, undo and rejection cases on the candidate.
gates.refusal: Do not claim full client conformance from a tool manifest or unauthenticated stub.

gates.claim: A desktop release artifact is approved for a supported target.
gates.contract: Artifact identity, installed lifecycle and applicable signing/update decisions match the release policy.
gates.evidence: Record exact artifact and commit, integrity, install/upgrade/recovery, decision status and author approval.
gates.refusal: An unsigned or untested artifact cannot be described as signed, distributed or approved.

gates.claim: Desktop release sign-off asserts quality, security or accessibility.
gates.contract: Applicable release gates and explicit failure or waiver policy are satisfied for the candidate matrix.
gates.evidence: Retain candidate and target identifiers, gate outcomes, manual gaps and any authorized waiver.
gates.refusal: Do not substitute historical results, hidden failures or an undocumented waiver for release evidence.

gates.claim: Desktop release sign-off includes required support documentation and any claimed guide, sample or public presentation.
gates.contract: Required release documentation is complete and released materials truthfully describe the supported candidate and respect artifact rights.
gates.evidence: Inspect required documentation and applicable links, samples, captions, credits, privacy and claim-to-evidence mapping.
gates.refusal: Do not sign off without required documentation or accept an uninspected material or claim merely because a link is published.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained Bible and series work.
gates.contract: All retained planning, series, relationships and generated-proposal scope has applicable accepted contracts.
gates.evidence: Link L06's complete retained acceptance and exact-candidate results, including independent optional use cases.
gates.refusal: Optional review or casting exclusion does not remove L06 from roadmap completion.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained history and organization.
gates.contract: History, collections, recents, goals and source-anchored notes satisfy their retained contracts.
gates.evidence: Link L07's full retained acceptance, host integration and recovery evidence for the candidate.
gates.refusal: A core snapshot or goal slice alone cannot close the full retained lane.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained reader and continuity review.
gates.contract: The complete retained reader scope honors consent, exact citations, attribution and separate application.
gates.evidence: Link L09 acceptance, connected candidate results and applicable decisions, with provider and quality evidence distinguished.
gates.refusal: A planner, saved-record seam or optional-source exclusion alone cannot close the lane.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained audiobook and casting scope.
gates.contract: Applicable casting, generation, recovery and packaging decisions and contracts are accepted.
gates.evidence: Link L13's complete retained acceptance and approved, source-bound generation and recovery evidence.
gates.refusal: A narrator-only audition or unaccepted policy cannot close the retained audiobook lane.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained routing and spend policy.
gates.contract: Selected routes, admission, attribution and applicable cost modes are implemented under accepted policy.
gates.evidence: Link L14's full retained acceptance, dispatch and qualified enforcement evidence.
gates.refusal: An advisory preview or unknown price does not prove automatic routing or a strict cap.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained Android delivery.
gates.contract: The accepted Android storage, credential, lifecycle, voice and release scopes are met where retained.
gates.evidence: Link L18's complete target matrix, decisions, real-device results and authorized release evidence.
gates.refusal: An editor-only slice, emulator or open native decision cannot close the target lane.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete with retained glasses and companion delivery.
gates.contract: The approved private companion, tool and interaction contracts cover the retained target.
gates.evidence: Link L19's complete acceptance, accepted transport and real-hardware results.
gates.refusal: A mock, manifest or unapproved network path cannot close the hardware lane.

gates.claim: The requested roadmap is complete and includes desktop release sign-off.
gates.contract: The supported desktop matrix and candidate-specific release approval have been accepted.
gates.evidence: Link the L23 approval, exact artifact, matrix and candidate-specific gate record.
gates.refusal: Desktop sign-off alone cannot close other retained lanes or replace the direct L00–L23 conjunction.

gates.when: Review includes new 030 planning records; selected manuscript-only review does not require them.
gates.claim: A structured review includes new planning records.
gates.contract: Only the selected planning records use their explicit source scope, identity and version contract.
gates.evidence: Record consent, selected records, exact revisions and missing or changed-source behavior.
gates.refusal: Exclude unselected planning data; manuscript-only review does not wait for new planning records.

gates.when: An accepted future review slice uses routing policy; manual provider/model selection does not require routing.
gates.claim: An accepted future structured review slice uses routing policy.
gates.contract: The specific accepted policy preserves explicit route authority, attribution and applicable admission limits.
gates.evidence: Test selected policy, actual route, consent and unknown-charge behavior for that review slice.
gates.refusal: Do not infer automatic routing; manually selected review does not wait for routing policy.

gates.when: Casting references new 030 character records; narrator-only generation does not require them.
gates.claim: An audiobook cast references new character records.
gates.contract: Only the explicitly selected character identities and revisions enter the approved cast.
gates.evidence: Test selected records, approved mapping, changed or unavailable characters and source-bound output.
gates.refusal: Do not infer permission to use all characters; narrator-only generation does not wait for them.
